entities.title: The Worker
entities.summary: The Cloudflare Worker at cyberspace-explorer.com: it serves the page, signs readers in with GitHub and reads GitHub for them, serves what the crawler collected, and runs /admin, where the crawler's list is edited.
entities.purpose: Lets a reader read private GitHub repositories in the page without the page ever holding their GitHub access: the token stays in a sealed, HttpOnly cookie and only this code adds it to GitHub calls.
boundaries: The page itself is ../index.html, imported as text by index.js; this folder only serves it.
With a reader's token it reads GitHub and nothing else, and only the paths the page needs; GitLab, and readers who paste a token, never go through it.

With its own bindings it shares the crawler's database, bucket and queue (space.js): it serves the crawler's views at /api/space, asks for rescans when a player approaches stale data, and lets the logins in ADMIN_LOGINS change the address list and settings at /admin. It never scans anything itself.
Without its three secrets /auth/me says sign-in isn't set up and starting a sign-in answers 503; the page then falls back to pasted tokens.

No dependencies: app.js and space.js run in Workers and in Node, which is how test/app.test.js and test/space-api.test.js run them. space.js imports the crawler's data layer (crawler/src/store.js, address.js), which has none either.
